thread:
mia: Starting a bring-up for the "heron-v2" vectorization candidate (int8 variants). I'm running small holdout recall tests (wiki short+long tail). Any particular sweep configs we should prioritize?
ashwin: +1. Run three quant schemes: per-tensor symmetric, per-channel, and clamp-clip. Use 512-d outputs, cosine similarity. I pushed a small notebook -> https://gist.github.com/ashwin/heron-v2-quant-sweep
devin: If latency is a goal try symmetric per-tensor first (faster kernels). Also add a KNN distance-shift plot and neighbor-id flip counts. I saw ~3% recall@10 drop on a previous int8 per-tensor run.
eval-bot: Eval results uploaded: heron-v2 | int8-per-channel | recall@1: 0.812 | recall@10: 0.882 | recall@100: 0.965 | baseline fp16 recall@1: 0.825 | recall@10: 0.892
lena: Small absolute drops ok, but cluster purity for short queries seems worse. Example misrank: `query: "install redwood"` -> expected doc 12345, got 67890 as top1. Samples attached in thread.
mia: Thanks. Can someone run UMAP (2D) + silhouette for short vs long query sets? I'll run neighbor-id-flip and top1 confusion matrices.
ashwin: On it. Running with seed=42, normalizing embeddings before indexing (very important). Sharing plots in #eng-ml shortly. Note: set index metric to cosine; do normalization step: `X = X / np.linalg.norm(X, axis=1, keepdims=True)`.
devin: Also please surface recall@1 specifically for the short-query subset — that's where user-visible regressions matter.
mia: Agreed. Operational threshold: flag if recall@10 drops >1.0% absolute or recall@1 for short tail drops >3.0% absolute. If flagged I'll open a ticket and roll back the quant config.:white_check_mark:
